h: Smart moves for a Derby climbing session
p: Here's a tip that seasoned climbers swear by: climb with your legs, not your arms. It sounds obvious, but first-timers tend to haul themselves up by their hands and run out of puff after three walls. Push up through your feet, keep your arms fairly straight where you can, and you'll last the whole session. Little ones get the hang of this surprisingly quickly once someone points it out.

A couple of practical bits before the day. Everyone climbing needs a participation form completing, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, so it's worth doing online at home. There's usually a minimum age for climbers and rules on supervising younger kids, which you'll find when you book. Allow about two hours all in, including arrival, harness fitting and the briefing.
What to bring? Water, trainers, comfortable clothes and a hair bobble. What not to bring? Rings, a heavy lunch in your stomach and any expectation that you'll feel your arms tomorrow morning.

Derby has plenty more to fill a day. Markeaton Park, on the west side of the city, is big and lively with play areas and space to run about, and Darley Abbey Park follows the River Derwent north from the centre for a lovely riverside walk. Football fans will know Pride Park, home of Derby County, and the city's Cathedral Quarter is a good spot to finish with food.
